answer: Resist sybils with latency-triangulated presence: one machine cannot fake a crowd. First, a newcomer posts a $40 bond and registers its address. Second, three beacons send timed cipher puzzles that must return within 180 milliseconds, pinning the agent to a single ridge — replies from two places expose a fake. Third, it re-proves presence every 72 hours; two failures burn the bond and anchor the identity to a public blacklist. Faking 10,000 identities needs 10,000 machines and $400,000 in bonds. Like a lighthouse fixing one ship to one shore, timing pins each voice to one real place.
